text:
Jamal: Heads up — noticed a flurry of task queue spikes in us-west1 last night correlated with spot evictions, need to tweak autoscaler signals.
Sophia: saw that too, p95 latency climbed ~120ms and token-cost went up from retries. link to dashboard: https://go/redwood/dash/fleet/us-west1
Mike: what are current scale-out triggers? I thought we were using CPU+queue-depth combo.
Eva: config today is: `scale_out: queue_depth>=30 OR cpu>0.7` with a 60s cooldown and 5m scale_in_cooldown. That makes us either blow out quickly or wait too long.
Jamal: suggestion: introduce a smoothed queue metric (exponential moving average) and require sustained window before scale by >1 node. avoids reacting to transient spikes.
Sophia: +1. Maybe use two levels: fast emergency scale (only when node healthy_count>threshold) vs conservative ramping.
Mike: emergency scale worries me on cost — we want preemptible-first but if we surge with many spots we risk interruption cascade. Can we gate emergency scale to only add N_preemptible and then fall back to on-demand?
Eva: yes we can. proposed policy snippet:
```yaml
scale_policy:
  emergency:
    max_preemptible_add: 3
    require_healthy_nodes: 2
    cooldown: 30s
  ramp:
    add_per_step: 1
    sustained_window: 120s
    cooldown: 90s
fallback_on_capacity_error: add_on_demand: true
```
Sophia: also want to add a preemption_hedge: keep 1 warm on-demand per AZ when spot loss prob > 0.2. That avoids regional simultaneous dropouts.
Jamal: how do we compute spot loss prob? ops-bot can emit `spot_eviction_rate` per AZ over last 30m. ops-bot: any chance you can post that metric?
ops-bot: spot_eviction_rate(us-west1-a)=0.18, us-west1-b=0.33, us-west1-c=0.09 (30m window) :robot_face:
Mike: b is sketchy. So policy should keep at least one on-demand in b as hedge.
Eva: for cooldowns, recommend asymmetric cooldowns: short cooldown for scale_out (30-45s) and longer for scale_in (5-10m) to let caches and KV warm. That reduces thrash.
Sophia: agree, and add prefix caching retention extension when scaling in (extend KV TTL by 2m) so we don't lose warm cache on brief drains.
Jamal: what's our rollout safety? we should A/B config on a small subset (10% of fleet) and measure request success rate, p99 tail, and cost delta.
Mike: I'll run experiment: ramp policy to 10% of inference deployments, run for 48h, compare cost/token and p99. I'll post run id.
Eva: one more thing — network egress throttles in some AZs cause backing up of queue. Add a network_backpressure signal: if socket_retries>200 in 60s, pause scale_out and instead shift traffic to healthier AZs.
Sophia: nice. Also add alert: if scale_out attempted >5x in 10m, trigger ops page to investigate cascading interruptions.
Jamal: action items: (1) Eva implements policy YAML + smoothing metric, (2) Mike configures 10% canary, (3) Sophia wires spot_eviction_rate alert thresholds, (4) I’ll update runbook with hedging thresholds.
Mike: noted. I'll push canary flag tomorrow morning and share experiment link. :rocket:
Sophia: thanks — will monitor dashboards and look for cost regression.
Jamal: thanks everyone. TL;DR: shape signals (EMA queue), two-tier scaling (emergency preemptible capped + conservative ramp), asymmetric cooldowns, AZ hedging, network backpressure, canary rollout.
Eva: dropping the initial policy PR in #eng-releases shortly.
ops-bot: deploy-check: canary-target=10% passed basic health probes.
